findings.explanation: adaptive_protection_config (line 9-17) and advanced_options_config (line 20-26) are correctly gated behind `var.type == "CLOUD_ARMOR"`, and the variable descriptions document this restriction. But the preconfigured_waf_rules dynamic block (line 47) and rate_limit_rules dynamic block (line 96) have no such gate — they fire for any `var.type`. Per GCP's own Cloud Armor docs, edge security policies (CLOUD_ARMOR_EDGE) only support filtering on origin.asn/ip/region_code and request.headers/method/path/query/scheme — evaluatePreconfiguredExpr() (used by every preconfigured_waf_rules entry) and rate_limit_options are not in that list, and the docs' feature matrix indicates neither edge nor network policies support preconfigured WAF rules or rate limiting. A caller setting type = "CLOUD_ARMOR_EDGE" (a real, documented use case per this module's own variable description: "CLOUD_ARMOR_EDGE (Cloud CDN / Media CDN)") while also passing preconfigured_waf_rules or rate_limit_rules will build a plan GCP is likely to reject at apply — I could not confirm from public docs whether the API hard-rejects this or silently accepts and no-ops the unsupported rules; either outcome is bad (broken deploy, or a caller believing WAF/rate-limit protection is active when it silently isn't).
findings.remediation: Add a variable validation (on preconfigured_waf_rules and/or rate_limit_rules, or a top-level check) that fails fast with a clear error when var.type != "CLOUD_ARMOR" and either list is non-empty, mirroring the existing restriction already documented for adaptive_protection/advanced_options_config.
findings.title: preconfigured_waf_rules and rate_limit_rules are not gated to CLOUD_ARMOR, but GCP doesn't support them on CLOUD_ARMOR_EDGE/CLOUD_ARMOR_NETWORK policies

findings.explanation: This rule entry sets `preview = true`, which per Cloud Armor semantics means the rule is evaluated and logged but its `action` (deny(403), the module's default) is never actually enforced — yet `description = "Block vulnerability scanner traffic"` states the opposite. This is this repo's own reference implementation (README explicitly points people at example/examplea as "a complete, deployable reference"), so anyone copying it as-is inherits a WAF rule that looks like it blocks scanner traffic but doesn't. A rules engine can't catch this — it requires correlating the preview flag's semantics against the free-text description.
findings.remediation: Either drop `preview = true` if blocking scanner traffic is actually intended, or fix the description to reflect preview-only status (e.g. "Preview: log vulnerability scanner traffic — not yet blocking, evaluate false-positive rate before enabling").
findings.title: Example's scannerdetection WAF rule is preview-only (logs, doesn't block) but its description says "Block"

suggested_policies.dsl_extension_note: Turned out unnecessary — holden already had an if_equals (when/then) conditional primitive plus not_any/any for iterating repeated nested blocks. My original assessment that this needed a new DSL feature was wrong; I hadn't actually checked internal/policy/policy.go's ResourcePolicy struct before writing that claim. Implemented as HLD_GCP_454 in the holden repo (policies/gcp/compute/security-policy-type-rule-compatibility.yaml), with fixture tests/fixtures/gcp-cloud-armor-type-rule-compat/main.tf and TestGCPCloudArmorTypeRuleCompat in internal/policy/gcp_proposed_test.go. go test and golangci-lint clean; committed to JamesWoolfenden/holden main.
suggested_policies.rationale: The module-level finding above (HOLDEN_AI_001) is a general GCP Cloud Armor pattern, not specific to this repo: any Terraform config that sets a security policy's type to CLOUD_ARMOR_EDGE or CLOUD_ARMOR_NETWORK while also defining a rule using evaluatePreconfiguredExpr() or a rate_limit_options block will hit the same GCP-side incompatibility. coverage_by_type["google_compute_security_policy"] only has HLD_GCP_166 (deny-rule-beyond-default check), which doesn't touch this.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_454
name: Cloud Armor CLOUD_ARMOR_EDGE/CLOUD_ARMOR_NETWORK policies must not use preconfigured WAF rules or rate limiting
principle: governance
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  CLOUD_ARMOR_EDGE and CLOUD_ARMOR_NETWORK security policies don't support
  evaluatePreconfiguredExpr() WAF rules or rate_limit_options — GCP's own docs
  restrict edge policies to origin.asn/ip/region_code and request.headers/
  method/path/query/scheme matching only. A policy of either type carrying a
  rule with a preconfigured WAF expression or rate_limit_options will fail to
  apply, or worse, silently not enforce the rule the author believes is active.
remediation: |
  Only use type = "CLOUD_ARMOR" when any rule needs evaluatePreconfiguredExpr()
  or rate_limit_options. For CLOUD_ARMOR_EDGE/CLOUD_ARMOR_NETWORK, restrict
  rules to IP/geo/header/method/path/query/scheme matching.
resources:
  google_compute_security_policy:
    all:
      - if_equals:
          path: type
          value: "CLOUD_ARMOR_EDGE"
          then:
            path: rule
            not_any:
              any:
                - path: match.expr.expression
                  matches: "evaluatePreconfiguredExpr"
                - path: rate_limit_options
                  not_null: true
      - if_equals:
          path: type
          value: "CLOUD_ARMOR_NETWORK"
          then:
            path: rule
            not_any:
              any:
                - path: match.expr.expression
                  matches: "evaluatePreconfiguredExpr"
                - path: rate_limit_options
                  not_null: true
